questions.question: Which of the following books is authored by Indu Sundaresan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Feast of Roses**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The Feast of Roses:-**

 
 
• **It is a 2003 novel by Indian author Indu Sundaresan. (Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
• It is the sequel to her debut novel, The Twentieth Wife, and tells the story of Mehrunnisa, the twentieth and last wife of Mughal Emperor Jahangir, who came to be known as Empress Nur Jahan.
 
• The Feast of Roses is a lush and evocative novel that brings to life the opulence and intrigue of the Mughal court.
 
• It is also a story of love, betrayal, and ambition, as Mehrunnisa navigates the treacherous world of politics and power.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Secret of the Nagas:-**

 
 
• It is the second book in the Shiva Trilogy by Amish Tripathi.
 
• It is a fantasy novel set in the fictional land of Meluha and follows the story of Shiva, a Tibetan immigrant who is prophesied to be the destroyer of evil.
 
 
 
• **The One You Cannot Have:-**
 
 
• It is a novel by Preeti Shenoy about unrequited love and the challenges of finding true love.
 
• The story follows four characters: Aman, Shruti, Anjali, and Rishabh.
 
 
 
• **Ajaya: Rise of Kali:-**
 
 
• It is a novel by Amish Tripathi, the third and final book in the Shiva Trilogy.
 
• It is a fantasy novel set in the fictional land of Meluha, and follows the story of Shiva, a Tibetan immigrant who is prophesied to be the destroyer of evil.

questions.question: Respect for the National Flag and National Anthem is a ______ of every Indian citizen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Duty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Respect for the National Flag and National Anthem is a fundamental duty of every Indian citizen.**
 
• This is enshrined in Article 51A(a) of the Constitution of India. The other fundamental duties are:
 
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our freedom struggle.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote social harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all Indians, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop the scientific temper and humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive to achieve excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
• It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Legal right:-**

 
 
• It is an interest accepted and protected by law.
 
• It is a claim that a person has against another person or against the state. Legal rights can be enforced through the courts.
 
 
 
• **The Directive Principles of State Policy:-**
 
 
• DPSPs are a set of guidelines for the government of India to follow in order to achieve social and economic justice for all citizens.
 
• They are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution of India, and are not enforceable by the courts.
 
• However, they are fundamental to the governance of the country and the government is obliged to strive to implement them.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental right:-**
 
 
• Fundamental rights are essential for the protection of individuals from the state and from other individuals.
 
• 
 
The fundamental rights enshrined in the Constitution of India are: Right to equality, Right to freedom, Right against exploitation, Right to freedom of religion, Cultural and educational rights, and Right to constitutional remedies.

questions.question: What was the purpose behind the Pillars of Ashoka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To spread the dharma policies.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Pillars of Ashoka were used to spread the Dharma policies of Ashoka the Great. **
 
• Ashoka was a devout Buddhist, and he believed that the Dharma, or Buddhist teachings, were essential for creating a more just and peaceful society.
 
• He used the pillars to promulgate his Dharma policies, which included:
 
 
• **Non-violence and compassion for all living beings**
 
• **Respect for all religions and cultures**
 
• **Tolerance and understanding**
 
• **Duty to elders and parents**
 
• **Generosity to the poor and needy**
 
 
 
• The Pillars of Ashoka were erected at strategic locations throughout his kingdom so that his subjects would be able to read and learn about his Dharma policies.
 
• Ashoka also sent out special officials, known as Dhamma Mahamattas, to spread the Dharma message and to ensure that his subjects were following his policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• List of the Pillars of Ashoka without images:-
 
 
• **Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, India**
 
• **Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh, India**
 
• **Lauriya-Nandangarh, Bihar, India**
 
• **Vaishali, Bihar, India**
 
• **Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh, India**
 
• **Topra Kalan, Haryana, India**
 
• **Rummindei, Nepal**
 
• **Kandahar, Afghanistan**
 
• **Mansehra, Pakistan**

questions.question: Which player was widely known by the name of Flying Sikh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Milkha Singh.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milkha Singh:-**

 
 
• **He is widely known by the name of the "Flying Sikh".**
 
• He was an Indian track and field sprinter who specialized in the 400 meters.
 
• He was the first Indian athlete to win a gold medal at the Asian Games and the Commonwealth Games in the 400 meters event.
 
• He also competed in the 1960 Summer Olympics, where he finished fourth in the 400 meters final, just 0.13 seconds behind the bronze medalist.
 
• Milkha Singh retired from athletics in 1966.
 
• **He was awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth highest civilian honor, in 1959, and the Padma Bhushan, India's third highest civilian honor, in 2001. He died in 2021 at the age of 91.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Arshdeep Singh:-**

 
 
• He is a young Indian cricketer who is quickly making a name for himself.
 
• He is a left-arm medium-fast bowler and left-handed lower-order batter. 
 
• He made his debut for Punjab in domestic cricket in 2018 and was picked up by the Punjab Kings in the Indian Premier League (IPL) auction the same year.
 
 
 
• **Harbhajan Singh:-**
 
 
• He is one of the greatest off-spinners to have ever played cricket.
 
• He is known for his guile, wicket-taking ability, and aggressive style of bowling.
 
• Harbhajan was a part of the Indian team that won the 2007 T20 World Cup and the 2011 ODI World Cup.
 
• He is also the only bowler to have taken a hat-trick in all three formats of the game.
 
 
 
• **Yuvraj Singh:-**
 
 
• He is one of the most iconic cricketers of all time.
 
• He is known for his all-round ability, his big-match performances, and his fighting spirit.
 
• Yuvraj played a major role in India's victory in the 2007 T20 World Cup and the 2011 ODI World Cup.
 
• He was named the Player of the Tournament in the 2011 World Cup, where he scored 362 runs and took 15 wickets.

• The dance movements are energetic and expressive, and they depict the joy and gratitude of the community for the harvest.

questions.question: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA):-**

 
 
• **It was founded in 1928. (Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• It was a revolutionary organization that emerged from the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) in response to the rise in anti-colonial sentiment in India.
 
• **The HSRA was inspired by socialist and Marxist ideals, and it advocated for a revolution to overthrow British rule and establish a socialist republic.**
 
• Some of the most prominent members of the HSRA included Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Sukhdev Thapar, and Rajguru.
 
• The HSRA carried out a number of daring attacks against the British government, including the Kakori train robbery and the assassination of British police officer John Saunders.
 
• The HSRA was eventually suppressed by the British government, but its legacy continues to inspire revolutionaries and activists around the world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Kotwal Dasta**
 
• **Gadar Party**
 
• **Berlin Committee**
 
• **Indian National Army (INA)**

questions.question: What is the capital of India's neighbouring country Afghanistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kabul**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kabul:-**

 
 
• **It is the capital and largest city of Afghanistan.**
 
• It is located in the eastern part of the country, at an altitude of 1,790 meters (5,873 ft), in a narrow valley surrounded by the Hindu Kush mountains along the Kabul River.
 
• Kabul has been inhabited for over 3,500 years and has been the capital of many different empires and kingdoms throughout its history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kandahar:-**

 
 
• **It is the second largest city in Afghanistan, located in the south of the country on the Arghandab River. **
 
• It is the capital of Kandahar Province and the center of the larger cultural region called Loy Kandahar. 
 
 
 
• **Kathmandu:-**
 
 
• **It is the capital and largest city of Nepal. **
 
• Kathmandu is a multicultural city with a population of over 4 million people.
 
• The majority of the population is Newari, but there are also significant Nepali, Tamang, and Sherpa minorities.
 
• The city is also home to a small number of Hindus, Sikhs, and Christians.
 
 
 
• **Karachi:-**
 
 
• **It is the capital city of the Pakistani province of Sindh.**
 
• It is the largest city in Pakistan and 12th largest in the world, with a population of over 20 million.
 
• It is situated at the southern tip of the country along the Arabian Sea coast.

questions.question: Which of the following is “NOT” a biosphere reserve in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gir Forest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gir Forest:-**

 
 
• **It is a forest, national park, and wildlife sanctuary near Talala Gir in Gujarat, India. Gir Forest is not a biosphere reserve.**
 
• It is located 43 km (27 mi) north-east of Somnath, 65 km (40 mi) south-east of Junagadh and 60 km (37 mi) south-west of Amreli.
 
• It is part of the Khathiar-Gir dry deciduous forests ecoregion.
 
 
 
• **Biosphere Reserve:-**
 
 
• It is a designated area of land or coastal environment that has been established to promote and demonstrate a balanced relationship between people and nature.
 
• Biosphere reserves are typically zoned into three areas: a core area, a buffer zone, and a transition zone.
 
• There are 18 biosphere reserves in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nilgiri:-**

 
 
• **The Nilgiri Mountains (also known as the Blue Mountains) are a mountain range in southern India, spread across the states of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala. **
 
• The highest peak in the Nilgiris is Doddabetta, which is 2,637 meters (8,652 feet) above sea level.
 
 
 
• **Sunderbans:-**
 
 
• **The Sundarbans is a mangrove forest in the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta, covering 10,000 square kilometres (3,900 sq mi) of land and water in both India and Bangladesh. **
 
• It is the world's largest mangrove forest, and is home to a unique variety of wildlife, including the Bengal tiger. 
 
 
 
• **Cold Desert:-**
 
 
• **It is a desert that is characterized by low temperatures and arid conditions. **
 
• Cold deserts are typically found at high altitudes, where the air is thinner and the temperature is colder.
 
• Cold deserts can also be found in regions that are in the rain shadow of mountains, where they do not receive much precipitation.

questions.question: “PM POSHAN” Scheme is implemented by which ministry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Ministry of Education.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman:-**

__
 
• **The PM POSHAN Scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Education. **
 
• It is a centrally sponsored scheme that provides one hot cooked meal to children in government and government-aided schools from pre-primary to class VIII.
 
• The scheme was launched in 2021-22 and is currently in its third year of implementation.
 
• The two main objectives of the PM POSHAN scheme are to:
 
 
• **Improve the nutritional status of children in Government and Government-aided schools from Class 1 to 8.**
 
• **Encourage poor children, especially those from disadvantaged sections, to attend school and help them concentrate on classroom activities.**
 
 
 
• Some of the benefits of the PM POSHAN scheme are as follows:-
 
 
• **It helps to improve the nutritional status of children.**
 
• **It encourages children to attend school and helps them concentrate on classroom activities.**
 
• **It improves the health and development of children.**
 
• **It enhances the future opportunities of children.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Women and Child Development (WCD):-**

 
 
• It is the apex body in the Government of India for formulation and administration of the rules and regulations and laws relating to women and child development in India. 
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment:-**
 
 
• MSJE is a Government of India ministry responsible for the welfare, social justice, and empowerment of disadvantaged and marginalized sections of society.
 
• The ministry was established in 1999 with the merger of the Ministry of Welfare and the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Women and Child Development:-**
 
 
• WCD is a branch of the Government of India that is responsible for the development and empowerment of women and children, and for ensuring their protection from all forms of violence and exploitation.

questions.question: Which of the following article of Indian constitution is related with “Promotion of International Peace and security”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 51.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51:-**

 
 
• Article 51 of the Constitution of India is a directive principle of state policy enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• It reflects India's commitment to international peace and cooperation, and outlines the guiding principles for the country's foreign policy objectives.
 
• The article states that the **"State shall endeavour to promote international peace and security, to maintain just and honourable relations between nations, to foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and to encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration."**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 40:-**

 
 
• It states that the** "State shall take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government."**
 
 
 
• **Article 47:-**
 
 
• It states that the **"State shall regard the raising of the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties and, in particular, the State shall endeavor to bring about prohibition of the consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and of drugs which are injurious to health."**
 
 
 
• **Article 43:-**
 
 
• It states that the **"State shall endeavour to secure, by suitable legislation or economic organisation or in any other way, to all workers, agricultural, industrial or otherwise, work, a living wage, conditions of work ensuring a decent standard of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities and, in particular, the State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas."**

questions.question: Indian musician Jagjit Singh is credited for the revival of ______ genre of music / poetry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghazal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jagjit Singh:-**

 
 
• He was born on February 8, 1941, in Lahore, Punjab. 
 
• He received his bachelor's degree in English literature from Delhi University.
 
• **Jagjit Singh is credited for the revival of the ghazal genre of music and poetry. (Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
• Jagjit Singh has been awarded numerous awards for his singing, including the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and National Awards. He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2002.
 
• ​Some of his most famous ghazals include:
 
 
• Aaj Phir Tumko Dekha To
 
• Tumse Milne Ko Jee Chahta Hai
 
• Dil Mein Tu Hai
 
• Mere Dil Mein Tum Hi Ho
 
• Woh Kaun Si Gali Hai
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghazals:-**

 
 
• These are a form of lyric poetry originating in the Arabic-speaking world.
 
• They are typically short poems, consisting of five to fifteen rhyming couplets.
 
• Each couplet is independent, but the ghazal as a whole has a thematic unity.
 
• Ghazals often deal with themes of love, longing, separation, and the pain of loss.
 
 
 
• **Sufism:-**
 
 
• It is a mystical tradition within Islam.
 
• It emphasizes introspection, spiritual closeness with God, and the purification of the soul.
 
• Sufis seek to achieve direct personal experience of God through a variety of practices, including prayer, meditation, and chanting.
 
 
 
• **Jazz:-**
 
 
• It is a music genre that originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans, Louisiana, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with its roots in blues and ragtime.
 
• Jazz is characterized by swing and blue notes, complex chords, call and response vocals, polyrhythms and improvisation. Jazz has roots in European harmony and African rhythmic rituals.

questions.question: The “Double Dome” feature of Indo - Islamic architecture was introduced by which dynasty of Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lodi Dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Double Dome:-**

 
 
• **The double dome consists of two domes, one inner and one outer, with a space between them. **
 
• The inner dome is smaller and supports the weight of the outer dome. This design allows for taller and more slender domes, and it also creates a dramatic visual effect.
 
• **The Lodi dynasty introduced the "double dome" feature of Indo-Islamic architecture. **
 
• The first example of a double dome in Indo-Islamic architecture is the tomb of Sikandar Lodi (1517/18) in Delhi. Other notable examples include the tomb of Humayun (1572) in Delhi, the Taj Mahal (1648) in Agra, and the Jama Masjid (1656) in Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Lodi dynasty:-**
 
 
• It was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1451 to 1526.
 
• During their reign, they made significant contributions to Indo-Islamic architecture, including the introduction of the double dome.
 
• The Lodi style of architecture is characterized by its simplicity, elegance, and use of high-quality materials.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slave Dynasty:-**

 
 
• **It was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, which ruled over northern India from 1206 to 1290. **
 
• The dynasty was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, who was a former slave of the Ghurid Sultan Muhammad of Ghor. 
 
 
 
• **Khilji Dynasty:-**
 
 
• **It was the second dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling over northern India from 1290 to 1320. **
 
• The dynasty was founded by Jalal-ud-din Firoz Khilji, who was a former slave of the Mamluk dynasty.
 
• Jalal-ud-din was a skilled and ambitious general, and he quickly rose through the ranks of the Mamluk military.
 
• In 1290, he assassinated the last Mamluk sultan and seized control of Delhi for himself.
 
 
 
• **Tughlaq Dynasty:-**
 
 
• **It was the third dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling over northern India from 1320 to 1413. **
 
• The dynasty was founded by Ghazi Malik, who ascended the throne under the title of Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq.
 
• The Tughlaq Dynasty was a period of great expansion and consolidation for the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an artificial ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aquariums**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Artificial ecosystems:-**

 
 
• These are ecosystems that are created and maintained by humans.
 
• They are not self-sustaining, meaning that they require human intervention to survive.
 
• Examples of artificial ecosystems:
 
 
• **Aquariums (Hence option 1 is correct)**
 
• **Zoos**
 
• **Botanical gardens**
 
• **Greenhouses**
 
• **Farms**
 
• **Cities**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grasslands:-**

 
 
• **These are areas where the vegetation is dominated by grasses. **
 
• They are found on all continents except Antarctica and cover about 40% of the Earth's land surface.
 
• Grasslands are characterized by their open, treeless landscapes and their diverse plant and animal life. 
 
 
 
• **Desert:-**
 
 
• **A desert is a region of land that receives very little precipitation. **
 
• Deserts are found on all continents except Antarctica and cover about one-third of the Earth's land surface. 
 
 
 
• **Coral reefs:-**
 
 
• **These are underwater ecosystems made up of tiny living organisms called coral polyps. **
 
• Coral polyps are related to jellyfish and anemones. They live in colonies and secrete a hard limestone skeleton that builds up over time to form coral reefs.

questions.question: Which of the following has been awarded “Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021” for Wrestling?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi Kumar Dahiya.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ravi Kumar Dahiya:-**

questions.question: The point on the surface, nearest to the focus of the earthquake, is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **epicentre**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epicenter:-**

 
 
• **The focus, also known as the hypocenter, is the point within the Earth where an earthquake rupture starts.**
 
• The epicenter is the point on the surface directly above the focus.
 
• Seismic waves radiate in all directions from the focus, but they reach the epicenter first.
 
• This is why the epicenter is often the site of the most severe damage from an earthquake.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61f2967524b4c9842ee7f9dfaf7cb9e8d4cadb14dd5a843e3a9966600e025ac9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypocentre:-**

 
 
• Hypocentre of an earthquake is the point beneath the Earth's surface where the earthquake rupture begins.
 
• It is also known as the focus of the earthquake.
 
• The hypocentre is the source of the seismic waves that are generated by the earthquake.

questions.question: Which among the following festivals is associated with Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Solung**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Solung**:-

 
 
• **Solung is the most popular festival of the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, India. (Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• It is a post-harvest festival celebrated at the beginning of September every year to give thanks to the gods for a bountiful harvest and to pray for good fortune in the coming year.
 
• The main highlight of the Solung festival is the Ponung dance, a traditional Adi dance performed by women of all ages. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ugadi:-**

 
 
• **It is a Hindu festival that marks the beginning of the new year in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka in India. **
 
• This typically falls in late March or early April of the Gregorian calendar.
 
• It also falls during the Tamil month of either Panguni or Chithrai, sometimes on the day after Amavasya with 27th Nakshatra Revati.
 
 
 
• **Pongal:-**
 
 
• **It is a four-day Hindu harvest festival celebrated by the Tamil people of India and Sri Lanka. **
 
• It is dedicated to the sun god, Surya, and corresponds to Makar Sankranti, the harvest festival under many regional names celebrated throughout India.
 
 
 
• **Wangala:-**
 
 
• **This festival is celebrated in Meghalaya.**
 
• It is also known as the "100 Drum Festival".
 
• The festival is practised by the Garo tribe.

 It is celebrated in the honour of Misi Saljong, the Great River.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was established when 72 delegates from all over the country met at Bombay in December ______.

questions.question: Gangaur festival of Rajasthan is associated with which god and goddess?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Lord Shiva and Goddess Parwati.**__

• **Gangaur festival :-**

 
 
• **The Gangaur festival of Rajasthan is associated with the god Lord Shiva and the goddess Gauri, who is a manifestation of Parvati, Shiva's consort. **
 
• The name Gangaur is a combination of the words "Gan" and "Gaur", which refer to Shiva and Gauri respectively.
 
• **The Gangaur festival is celebrated in the spring season, during the month of Chaitra (March-April). **
 
• It is a colorful and joyous festival that celebrates the marital bond, fertility, and the arrival of spring.
 
• The festival is particularly popular among women, who dress up in their finest clothes and jewelry and participate in various rituals and celebrations.
 
• The Gangaur festival is a time for women to come together and celebrate their womanhood.
 

 
 
• It is also a time to pray for marital bliss, fertility, and the well-being of their families.

questions.question: In which type of farming the land is used for growing food and fodder crops and rearing livestock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Mixed farming.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mixed farming:-**

 
 
• It is a type of agriculture that combines the production of crops and livestock on the same farm.
 
• **The type of farming in which the land is used for growing food and fodder crops and rearing livestock is called mixed farming. (Hence option 2 is correct)**
 
• It is a sustainable and efficient system that can provide a variety of benefits, including:
 
 
• **Increased income and productivity**: Mixed farms can generate income from both crop and livestock sales, and the two enterprises can often complement each other. For example, the manure produced by livestock can be used to fertilize crops, and the crops can provide feed for the livestock.
 
• **Improved soil health: **Mixed farming can help to improve soil health by rotating crops and using manure to fertilize the land. This can lead to increased crop yields and reduced erosion.
 
• **Reduced risk**: Mixed farming can help to reduce risk by diversifying the farm's income streams. If one enterprise fails, the other can help to support the farm.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plantation agriculture:-**

 
 
• **Plantation agriculture is a type of commercial farming in which a single crop is grown on a large scale. **
 
• Plantations are typically owned by a single company or government, and they employ labourers to work on the land.
 
 
 
• **Subsistence farming:-**
 
 
• **It is a type of agriculture in which farmers grow crops and raise livestock to meet their own needs and the needs of their families, with little or no surplus for sale. **
 
• Subsistence farming is practiced all over the world, but it is particularly common in developing countries.
 
 
 
• **Shifting cultivation:-**
 
 
• **It is a type of agriculture in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned while post-disturbance fallow vegetation is allowed to freely grow while the cultivator moves on to another plot. **
 
• The period of cultivation is usually terminated when the soil shows signs of exhaustion or, more commonly, when the field is overrun by weeds.
 
• The period of time during which the field is cultivated is usually shorter than the period over which the land is allowed to regenerate by lying fallow.
